cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Drop the Armor
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to lower their guard, stop performing strength, or admit what affects them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Over dinner you keep saying you're managing. What's hard about going home?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The silence. I leave the television on so it sounds occupied.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Could you ask me over instead of pretending you've got company?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cook. I promise I won't be miserable all evening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you invite me without that promise? I'd like to come even if you're miserable and we eat toast.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 rank prefixes do not alter can-you-invite requests; A5 gentle unconditional offer is strong D108 but not a sustained high-status permission tactic.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 TV explanation causes A3 real-company invitation; B4 cooking/no-misery performance causes A5 request to invite without it.

relationship.evidence: B2 admits loneliness and B4 offers hosting to make company feel deserved, plausibly keeping a guard while seeking connection.

heightening.evidence: B4 promise of cheer causes A5 to remove the condition and offer presence even with sadness and simple food.

specificity.evidence: A1 dinner and going home, B2 television/silence and A5 toast make the possible visit concrete.
